explain.say: Car engine blocks, pump bodies, manhole covers and bronze statues are all cast: liquid metal poured into a hollow and left to freeze. People have cast bronze for over five thousand years. Look at the steps of sand casting, still the most common way.

explain.say: A pattern, a copy of the part, is packed in sand and removed, leaving a cavity. Metal shrinks as it cools, so the pattern is made a little oversize. For aluminium, about 1.3 percent: a 200 millimetre part needs a 202.6 millimetre pattern. Why do you think steel needs more allowance than cast iron?

explain.say: Steel shrinks about 2 percent, grey cast iron only about 1. Now watch the metal freeze. See the cooling curve: pure aluminium falls to 660 degrees, then stays flat for minutes while it releases latent heat and solidifies. Only when it is all solid does it cool again.

explain.say: How long does freezing take? Chvorinov's rule says time is proportional to volume over surface area, squared. A 100 millimetre cube has V over A of 16.7 millimetres; with a mould constant of 2 seconds per square millimetre, it takes about 556 seconds, over 9 minutes. A 50 millimetre cube takes a quarter of that. Why does that matter?

explain.say: Because thick parts freeze last and shrink, sucking metal in. A riser, a big reservoir of liquid metal with a high V over A, freezes after the casting and feeds it, so no holes form. Great job! Exam tip: design the riser to freeze last, and place it next to the thickest section.

faq.a: A pattern is packed in sand to make a mould cavity, molten metal is poured in through a sprue and runners, and after it freezes the sand is broken away and the casting is cleaned and finished.

faq.q: What does a cooling curve show?
faq.a: Temperature against time as metal cools. A pure metal shows a flat step at its freezing point while latent heat is released; alloys freeze over a range of temperatures.
asks: cooling curve of a pure metal

faq.a: Metal shrinks as it solidifies. A riser holds extra liquid metal that freezes last and feeds the casting, so shrinkage holes form in the riser instead of the part.
asks: what is a riser in casting

faq.a: Extra size added to the pattern to make up for the metal shrinking as it cools, about 1 percent for grey cast iron, 1.3 for aluminium and 2 for steel, plus machining allowance where needed.
Solidification time equals a mould constant times volume over surface area squared. Chunky parts with little surface freeze slowly; thin plates freeze fast.

facts: Chvorinov's rule: solidification time is proportional to (V/A)².

quiz.say: Two castings in the same mould material: one has V over A of 10 millimetres, the other 20. How do their freezing times compare?

quiz.say: A steel part must be 500 millimetres long. With a 2 percent shrinkage allowance, how long is the pattern?
